question: What are the required documents and fee to transfer the ownership of a business permit in Davao City?
reference_answer: Transfer of business ownership requires an Application for Transfer of Ownership, notarized Deed of Transfer/Sale/Assignment, SPA or Board Resolution, valid IDs, property proof (Tax Declaration/Lease Contract), current original Mayor's Permit, and new DTI/SEC/CDA registration. A PHP 50.00 service fee applies.

1. Application for Transfer of Ownership (electro-mechanical) form [S1, S2]

For the application form, you need to submit it to the Business Bureau and pay the order of payment at the City Treasurer’s Office.

Regarding the fee, the Citizens' Charter does not provide specific information about the fee for transferring the ownership of a business permit. 1. Affidavit of Change of Name / Correction of Business Name (notarized) - Single Proprietorship (Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public)

[S2] The third requirement is to pay the order of payment at the City Treasurer’s Office.

answer:
The procedure and checklist of requirements for the partial retirement of a business permit line in Davao City are as follows:

1. Prepare the following documents:
   - Affidavit of Partial Retirement (notarized) stating the reason, effective date of retirement, and line of business to retire [S1]
   - Secretary Certificate / Board or Partnership Resolution (notarized) stating the effective date of retirement [S1]

2. Submit the documents and application form for Partial Retirement to the Business Bureau. Proceed to the District Treasurer’s Office for the approval of the application [S2].

3. The Business Bureau will process the application as follows:
   - Assess Application for Partial Retirement [S2]
   - Verify and encode the Application for Partial Retirement [S2]
   - Check and approve the Application for Partial Retirement [S2]
   - Tag and encode the Partial Retirement [S3]
   - Encode notations and print the Business Permit [S3]

The processing time for the Business Bureau is approximately 1 hour and 55 minutes [S2]. The responsible personnel are the Processing and Records Section Heads of the Business Bureau [S2, S3].

The citizen is responsible for notarizing the Affidavit of Partial Retirement and the Secretary Certificate / Board or Partnership Resolution [S1]. The notarization can be done by any Notary Public [S1].

3.4 Encode notations and print the Business Permit. [S3]

To obtain an Occupational Permit as a regular employee or a foreign worker, the following requirements are needed based on [S2] and [S3] from the Business Bureau's Citizens Charter 2026:

1. Submit an application for the Occupational Permit.
2. If the application is approved, download the Occupational Permit from the online portal at https://occupationalpermit.davaocity.gov.ph/ or wait for the link to be sent via email or SMS. For walk-in applicants, physically claim the hard copy of the Occupational Permit.
3. Pay the corresponding fee:
   - Php125 for new and renewal applications
   - Php156.25 for late renewal applications

The processing time for both online and onsite applications is approximately 14 minutes, while the total time to complete the process is around 33 minutes. If the application is denied, the applicant will receive the returned documents and may need to reapply.

Sa pagbalhin ug titulo sa yuta o propedad sa City Treasurer, ang mga hinwang nga mahitabo sa Transfer Tax ay nakalistado sa City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2. [S2, S3]

Ang mga hinwang nga mahitabo sa pagbalhin ug titulo sa yuta o propedad sa City Treasurer sa pamamagitan sa Real Property Tax Transfer Ownership sa kasabot sa mga kailangan nga dokumento ug prosedyurong nakalistado sa [S3]. 3. Real Property Transfer Tax Certification (Local Treasury Operations Officer IV or CTO District Treasurers) [S3]
4. Client signs the logbook as proof of Transfer Tax Certification release (Window 10, RPTD, CTO SP Office, or the respective District Offices) [S3]

Ang mga hinwang nga mahitabo sa pagbalhin ug titulo sa yuta o propedad sa City Treasurer sa pamamagitan sa Real Property Tax Transfer Ownership ay ma-compute sa City Treasurer's Office sa pamamagitan sa mga nakalistado sa [S3]. Ang mga hinwang nga mahitabo sa pagbalhin ug titulo sa yuta o propedad sa City Treasurer sa pamamagitan sa Real Property Tax Transfer Ownership ay ma-compute sa 15 minutes (Ticket Checker or Assigned Personnel) [S3].

answer:
To obtain a Real Property Tax (RPT) Clearance from the City Treasurer in Davao City, follow these steps:

1. First, present all required documents at the Real Property Tax Division, CTO Sangguniang Panlungsod (CTO Poblacion) or the respective CTO District Offices [S2].

2. Verify the documents, retrieve the payment history, and issue the Tax Order of Payment for the Tax Clearance Fee at Counter 8, Real Property Tax Division (CTO Sangguniang Panlungsod) [S2].

3. After paying the Tax Clearance Fee, present the Official Receipt for the issuance of Real Property Tax Clearance at Counter 8, Real Property Tax Division, CTO Sangguniang Panlungsod, or the respective CTO District Offices [S4].

4. Finally, generate the Tax Clearance and issue a claim stub [S4].

The fee for the Real Property Tax Clearance is not specified in the provided sources. For the most accurate and up-to-date fee information, please visit the City Treasurer's office or contact them directly.

General building contractors are taxed on gross receipts exceeding PHP 2 million at a rate of 60% of 1% of the total contract price, payable in equal annual installments within the project term. However, for contractors who undertake to furnish materials in the construction work, only the cost of such materials shall be deducted from their gross receipts for the purpose of determining the tax due. For the specific tax rates for contractors with gross sales/receipts less than PHP 2 million, please refer to [S2]. For other types of taxation, such as for lessors and dealers of real estate and banks and other financial institutions, please refer to [S3].

answer:
Ang buwis para sa mga car dealers sa Davao ay kinokwenta sa pamamagitan ng City Treasurer's Office. Ang impormasyon sa buwis na ito ay maaaring nakita sa Citizen's Charter ng City Treasurer sa mga dokumento na:

- [S3] City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf | printed page 214 | chunk DEV120-CTO-PDF0059-C005
- [S3] City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf | printed page 214 | chunk DEV120-CTO-PDF0060-C001

Sa mga car dealers, ang buwis ay nakakalipas sa 90% ng kanilang mga kita sa pagbebenta ng bagong sasakyan at original na bahagi. Ang impormasyon sa mga buwis na ito ay nakakatitig sa mga kita na:

- Php 0 - Php 100,000,000.00: Wala kang buwis dahil ang kita mo ay hindi masyadong mataas.
- Php 100,000,001.00 - Php 2,000,000,000.00: Ang buwis mo ay Php 2,000,000.00.
- Php 2,000,000,001.00 - Php 3,000,000,000.00: Ang buwis mo ay Php 12,402,500.00 plus 22.0% ng 1.0% ng kanilang mga kita sa excess ng Php 2,000,000,000.00.
- Php 3,000,000,001.00 at ulit na ibabaw: Ang buwis mo ay Php 14,602,500.00 plus 11% ng 1.0% ng kanilang mga kita sa excess ng Php 3,000,000,000.00.

Para sa mga spare parts ng sasakyan, ang buwis ay kinokwenta sa pamamagitan ng City Treasurer's Office sa pamamagitan ng impormasyon sa [S3] City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf | printed page 214 | chunk DEV120-CTO-PDF0059-C005. Ang mga spare parts na ito ay kinokwenta sa pamamagitan ng 1.5% ng kanilang mga kita. Ang mga spare parts na ito ay maaaring makakuha ng tax exemption kung mayroon silang valid at existing dealership agreement at kung hindi maaaring makakuha ng tax exemption, maaaring makakuha ng tax exemption kung ang kanilang mga spare parts ay hindi masyadong mataas.

answer:
The rental fees for public market stalls are calculated based on the class of the stall and the size, as specified in the City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf [S1, S2, S3].

For Class A, the rate per square meter per day is P 4. For Class B, it's P 6, for Class C, P 4, and for Class D, P 2. If a stall is a front corner stall or booth, a 20% surcharge will be added to the prescribed fees [S2]. If it's a front stall or booth, a 15% surcharge will be added [S2]. For inside corner stalls or booths, a 10% surcharge will be added [S2].

There is also an automatic increase of 15% every four years, computed based on the existing rates of fees to the increasing cost of maintenance operations [S2].

For delinquency in paying the monthly rentals for market stalls, a surcharge of twenty-five pesos (P 25) per day is applicable after the 20th day of the month [S3].

For the building floor area, the fee is Php 3.00 per square meter [S3].

answer:
Ang bayad sa Demolition Permit ay kinokwenta sa National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) na nakatanggap ng bagong Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR). Sa ilalim ng mga ito, ang bayad ay kinokwenta per square meter ng floor area ng bawat gusali ([S3]).

Para sa mga bawat metro kwadrado ng floor area, ang bayad ay Php 3.00 ([S3]).

Para sa mga building systems/frames o portion thereof per vertical o horizontal dimensions, including fences, ang bayad ay Php 4.00 ([S3]).

Para sa mga structures na may taas ng 10.00 meters o mas mataas, ang bayad ay kinokwenta every meter o portion thereof ([S3]).

Wala pong nakit-an nga impormasyon bahin sa bayad para sa mga gusali na may floor area above 10,000.00 sq.meters.

Sa iba pang mga transaksyon, maaari mong dahan-dahan pansinin ang Citizens' Charter ng BFP ([S1]) at ng Office of the City/Municipal Building Official (OCBO) ([S2]).

answer:
The legal difference between a Variance and an Exception when applying for additional allowable land use under the Zoning Ordinance is as follows:

1. Variance: This is a form of deviation which grants a property owner relief from certain provisions of the rules when strict compliance with physical standards/guidelines such as building height, area requirement, setback, and the like would result in unnecessary hardship or difficulty upon the owner due to the peculiar physical surroundings, shape, or topographical conditions of the property. [S1]

2. Exception: This is a form of deviation which grants a property owner relief from certain provisions of the rules when strict enforcement thereof would result in an unnecessary hardship or difficulty upon the owner. However, the Integrated Zoning Ordinance does not explicitly state that the property's peculiar physical surroundings, shape, or topographical conditions are a requirement for an Exception. Instead, it states that the Sangguniang Panlungsod may grant an Exception upon application of the project proponent and upon favorable recommendation by the Local Zoning Board of Appeals if strict enforcement of the rules would cause unnecessary hardship or difficulty. [S1, S3]

answer:
To secure a Locational Clearance for Business through the online BPLS portal, follow these steps:

1. Submit your application online [S2]. The City Planning and Development Office (CPDO) will evaluate your application [S2].

2. If your application is approved or conditionally approved, the Zoning Officer will update the BPLS system with the status of your application and stipulate any necessary conditions [S1, S2].

3. If your application is denied, the Zoning Officer will update the BPLS system with the status of the application and draft a Denial Letter [S1].

4. For the issuance of the Locational Clearance, you will need to provide the following documentary requirements offline:
   - A SPA (Sale/Purchase Agreement) from the building owner to process the application for Locational Clearance [S3, DO 4].
   - Seven (7) complete sets of Building Plans (original copy) with filled-up title blocks and signed and sealed by a CE/Architect [S3, DO 5].
   - A Certified True Copy of Title issued by the Registry of Deeds (ROD) or show the original copy of title for validation (1 original for validation, 1 photocopy) [S3, DO 6].
   - A Locational Clearance Application duly notarized and signed by the applicant (1 photocopy) [S3, DO 7].

answer: The BFP integrates with eBOSS backroom operations for one-time assessment and payment in Davao City through a shared information system with OSCP/BOSS. This process is outlined in [S1] and [S2] of the BFP-CITIZENS-CHARTER-2022.pdf document. For one-time assessment, the applicant will be given a queuing number and an Operations Support Paper (OPS) will be issued [S2]. For one-time payment, the payment will be collected and an Official Receipt (OR) will be issued [S1]. The processing time for both steps is a maximum of ten (10) minutes [S1, S2]. The Person Responsible for the Fire Code Assessment (FCA) will issue the OPS, and the Agency responsible for the backroom operation is OSCP/BOSS [S2]. The client can present the OPS and pay the corresponding Fire Code Fees indicated in the OPS to proceed to the releasing window to claim the stub by presenting the OR [S3].

answer:
Under RA 9514, businesses handling or storing flammable liquids and gases may require the following additional fire clearance permits:

1. For importers of these products, they are required to apply for either a Philippine Standard (PS) License (for manufacturers) or an Import Commodity Clearance (ICC) Certificate (for importers) [S1].

2. If the building/facilities/structures are required to install any or combination of the following:
   - Wet standpipe system;
   - Automatic fire suppression system; and
   - Automatic fire detection and alarm system, a Fire Safety Clearance (FSCR/FSCCR/FSMR) is required [S2].

3. For fire safety clearance during welding, cutting, and other hot work operations, a permit is required, especially during new construction or renovation [S3].

For more information, you may refer to the BFP Citizens' Charter 2022 available at BFP-CITIZENS-CHARTER-2022.pdf.
